text:
alex: Heads-up — we're seeing DNS failures from APAC edge clusters after the NAT IP rotation at ~06:40 UTC. Some pods on the same service resolve, others get NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL. Anyone else?
ops-bot: NAT rotation completed: egress-ngw-2 -> egress-tier-b (06:41 UTC) — change deployed by infra-automation.
maya: Confirming. Internal registry "registry.internal.svc" sometimes returns NXDOMAIN from gpu-az3 nodes, but resolves from gpu-az1.
samir: Can you paste /etc/resolv.conf and a quick dig? Are nodes running node-local-dns or using systemd-resolved stub?
alex: On affected node (gpu-az3-04):
```
$ cat /etc/resolv.conf
# Generated by systemd-resolved
nameserver 127.0.0.53
options edns0
search default.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
```
And dig:
```
$ dig +short registry.internal.svc @127.0.0.53
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 23892
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1
;; SERVER: 127.0.0.53#53(127.0.0.53)
```
maya: Interesting — some nodes show the IP fine. Might be stale negative cache or upstream rate-limiting by new egress IP.
lina: We recently observed a pattern where node-local-dns (and systemd-resolved stubs) will cache negative responses for the SOA negative-ttl and keep serving NXDOMAIN until expiry when upstream rotates IPs quickly. Could also be DNS provider refusing queries from the new NAT IP (geo/rate limit).
samir: Quick mitigation: restart node-local-dns daemonset on affected nodes or restart systemd-resolved to flush caches. Example: `kubectl rollout restart ds node-local-dns -n kube-system` or `systemctl restart systemd-resolved` on host.
alex: Restarted node-local-dns on 5/12 APAC nodes — those are now resolving. Still 7 nodes showing NXDOMAIN.
```
$ journalctl -u systemd-resolved -n 50 | tail -n 5
Mar 09 06:46:12 systemd-resolved[1123]: DNSSEC validation failed for registry.internal.svc IN A: SERVFAIL
Mar 09 06:46:14 systemd-resolved[1123]: Answer cached: NXDOMAIN (negative-ttl 3600s)
```
maya: That negative-ttl of 3600s explains why rest stay bad after single upstream transient error. We should reduce negative-cache TTL on node-local-dns or configure failover to kube-dns.
lina: Also check if EDNS0 or DNSSEC settings flipped during the egress change — some upstream resolvers reject EDNS and drop queries which shows as SERVFAIL. Any firewall logs from provider?
ops-bot: GPU-scaler: cordoned and rescheduled 20 pods from az3 -> az1 at 06:50 while nodes were being remediated.
samir: Short-term fix: patch node-local-dns config to fallthrough to kube-dns and set negative-cache-min to 30 (or negative-ttl override) so transient upstream errors don't last an hour. We'll push a configmap change + rollout. Example snippet:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  upstreams: |
    - 169.254.20.10 # kube-dns
    - 8.8.8.8
  negative-ttl: "30"
```
maya: Can we also add a probe in Console that checks per-region resolver success rate and NXDOMAIN spikes (per-route)? If provider is rate-limiting the rotated IP we'll want automated rollback.
alex: For immediate risk mitigation I've pinned critical GPU jobs to us-east and disabled new node scale-ups in APAC until we have provider confirmation. :thumbsup:
lina: I'll open a ticket with the DNS provider (include NAT rotation time + sample NXDOMAINs) and add monitor + postmortem. Samir — please include the config diff in the ticket.
samir: Will do. After config patch we'll roll through APAC and then change negative TTL cluster-wide. Expect a few minutes of flutter while caches rebuild.
maya: Thanks everyone. Follow-up: add a runbook item for NAT rotations that includes a resolver-smoke test and negative-cache TTL check.
alex: Agreed. Filing follow-ups now.
